title: Derive the install payload from the shipped directory

intentCoverage.report:
# Dough Intent Coverage: Derive the install payload from the shipped directory

**Verdict: Caught** (on the list-era to directory-release update path). Also noted: the fresh-install check `install-public-payload.sh` ran the faulted path and passed. That is an assertion gap on the fresh-install path.

- Story: `.planning/seeds/SEED-423-shrink-the-installed-distribution.md` section "Derive the install payload from the shipped directory". Plan: `.planning/slice-plans/796-derive-the-install-payload-from-the-shipped-directory/PLAN.md`.
- Revision: 80087ac3086625e928680a3d495d2526a3fd144f. Checked in an isolated detached scratch worktree, which has since been removed. The execution checkout was not edited.
- Promise checked: for a directory-format release, every regular file under `Distribution/src/skills/` is installed into both `.agents/skills` and `.claude/skills` with its tagged bytes. A change to the reviewed directory alone changes the client payload.

## Fault
`Distribution/src/install/open-dough-payload-inventory.sh`, `read_release_payload`. I changed `find . -type f` to `find . -type f -not -path "*/references/*"`. Every file under any `references/` directory is now silently left out, and install still succeeds. This is the caller's suggested "skip references/" variant, used as suggested. No fixtures or assertions were changed.

## Independent wrong-behavior observation
With the fault applied, I ran `install.sh --platform codex` from the scratch source into a fresh target.
- Install exited 0.
- The source tree has 375 files. Each of the two roots received 294.
- 81 `references/` files were missing from both `.agents/skills` and `.claude/skills`, for example `dough-execute-plan/references/admit-accepted-work.md`.

## Maintained checks
Command: `bash scripts/test.sh Distribution/tests/installation/install-public-payload.sh Distribution/tests/installation/update-list-to-directory-release.sh Distribution/tests/installation/payload-declaration-links.sh`. The runner's outcomes file showed the result for each check.

| Run | Exit | install-public-payload | payload-declaration-links | update-list-to-directory-release |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 0 | passed | passed | passed |
| Faulted | 1 | **passed** | **failed** | **failed** |
| Restored | 0 | passed | passed | passed |

- **The catch that matches the promise:** `Distribution/tests/installation/update-list-to-directory-release.sh:66`, the line `git show v0.1.2:Distribution/src/skills/dough-update/references/directory-only.md | cmp -s - "${root}/${directory_only}"`. This checks the tagged bytes, in each root, of a new file that only the directory entry names. It failed on the first root. The fixture is the release-source fixture built by that test: a list-era 0.1.1 updated by `apply` to a directory-format 0.1.2.
- **Also caught:** `Distribution/tests/installation/payload-declaration-links.sh:62` (`check_declared_links`). It printed many lines such as "declared dough-story-wrap-up/SKILL.md links to undeclared references/story-branch-integration.md". This catch is incidental: it holds only because shipped Markdown links into `references/`. It does not check what gets installed.
- **Not caught (assertion gap):** `install-public-payload.sh`, through `Distribution/tests/support/assert-public-payload-install.sh`. It ran the faulted install path and passed. Its expected list, `managed_files` in `Distribution/tests/helpers/public-payload-fixture.bash`, is built by calling the same `read_release_payload`. Its full-tree comparison (`actual_files == expected_files`) and `assert_payload_bytes_match` therefore shrink along with the fault. No check on that path compares against an independent listing of `Distribution/src/skills/`.

## Restoration
- An EXIT trap ran `git checkout --` on the faulted file.
- The post-probe `git status --porcelain` matched the pre-probe status byte for byte (both empty), and `git diff HEAD` was empty.
- The restored rerun passed all three checks.
- The scratch worktree was removed with `git worktree remove`.

## Next proof action
- No new proof is required for the promise on the update path. The catch at `update-list-to-directory-release.sh:66` holds.
- Optional, for the fresh-install path: make `assert-public-payload-install.sh` (or the fixture it uses) compare installed roots with an independent listing of `Distribution/src/skills/`, rather than with `read_release_payload`. That would turn this assertion gap into a catch.

Prior disposition: none of the evidence matches a planned repair. The fresh-install gap is a new observation from this probe. Whether to repair it is the caller's decision.

## Cost
- Test runtime (measured, wall-clock seconds from the shell around `scripts/test.sh`; per-job seconds come from the runner's times file):
  - Baseline: 8 s (jobs 7.9, 4.4, 1.4).
  - Faulted: 3 s (jobs 3.0, 1.1, 0.4).
  - Restored: 14 s (jobs 13.8, 7.9, ...).
  - The first baseline attempts, which ran before I captured outcomes, took about 17 s more.
  - `npm ci` in the scratch checkout took an unmeasured time of under a few minutes.
- Human effort: unavailable. No human interaction happened during this probe.
- Agent effort: unavailable. No token or turn counter is exposed to this agent. About 20 tool calls were made (a count, not a cost measure).


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 124415 ms (measured), from 1795476476884 to 1795476601299 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

## Wrap-up disposition

Checked revision 80087ac3086625e928680a3d495d2526a3fd144f. Verdict: caught on the list-to-directory update path (update-list-to-directory-release.sh:66); assertion gap on the fresh-install path (install-public-payload.sh derives its expectation through read_release_payload). Decision: no follow-up queued. The same fault already fails the ordinary installation group and CI through update-list-to-directory-release.sh, so the gap only moves detection earlier. The fixture coupling is recorded as process finding DD-636.
